basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma 'Cumque transissent septem dies, aquae diluvii inundaverunt terram. Septima dies sabbatum,'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: Cumque transissent septem dies, aquae diluvii inundaverunt terram. Septima dies sabbatum, id est, requiem, indicat vitae futurae. Cum ergo diluvium aquam baptismi significat, apte post septem dies ex quo arca facta est venit, quia in spe perpetuae quietis baptizamur. Cum vero fluctus tentationum aquae diluvii figurant, merito etiam tunc post septem dies veniunt, quia propter fidem ad spem futurorum bonorum, persecutionem justi patiuntur ab eis qui terrena miseri bona coelestibus, mansuris temporalia praeponunt. At vero diluvium cum adventui novissimi examinis assimilatur, etiam sic congruenter post dies septem terram inundat, quia tunc electi omnes qui jugum Christi suave et onus leve portaverunt inveniunt requiem animabus suis.
